modeLabels.dynamic: both players dynamic; existing carrier-moving contact sweep
modeLabels.kinematic: stationary carrier and kinematic defender moving at matched relative closing speed

method.rotationalEnergy: 0.5 times angular velocity squared in the composed world/principal-inertia frame, weighted by the engine-reported principal moments.
method.contactWork: Normal impulse work is impulse magnitude multiplied by the average pre/post relative point velocity projected on the contact normal. Rapier uses solver impulses; Jolt infers each pair impulse from pre/post relative normal point velocity and inverse mass, without direct solver-lambda access.
method.contactStepDefinition: contactStep means at least one player-player or player-ground manifold is active. tackleContactStep means a nonzero carrier-defender normal impulse. Ground support and player damping are present in nominally non-tackle-contact steps.
method.energyConservationLimit: Strictly contact-free gravity-only frames are checked against 0.05 J per step when present. These grounded scenarios currently have zero such frames, so the gravity-only conservation assertion has no empirical coverage. Non-tackle steps still include ground support, friction, damping, and measured normal impulses.
method.positionIntegration: Logged displacement is compared with post-step COM velocity times fixed dt; maximum accepted per-step residual is 0.05 m.

energyModel.kinematicEnergyNote: Kinematic defender KE/PE uses cached nominal dynamic mass and inertia for comparison; the prescribed body is an external motion/energy reservoir and is excluded from claims of closed-system conservation.
energyModel.potentialReference: Each body potential is zero at its first post-step COM height.

centralVerdict.rule: Compare defender kinetic-energy increase plus gravitational potential energy released by descent at the carrier-tilt peak with the absolute whole-system residual after normal-impulse work; this is a diagnostic bookkeeping comparison, not a calibrated physicality threshold.
centralVerdict.interpretation: The defender kinetic-energy increase plus potential energy released by descent exceeds the whole-system residual after measured normal-impulse work. This supports two-body energy transfer in this probe, but does not establish that the contact model is physically accurate.
